title: Label Annotation for Tabular Anomaly Detection with Large Language Models

problem.claim: Human-centric label annotation is a primary bottleneck for large-scale production systems in tabular anomaly detection.

gap.claim: LLM-based coarse-grained annotation remains difficult because semantic priors are not grounded in rigorous deduction and single-domain fine-tuning risks overfitting.

contributions.claim: A coarse-to-fine label annotation pipeline combines coarse-grained annotation with fine-grained human verification to improve labor efficiency.
TaDGeneral is a large-scale cross-domain corpus constructed by fusing deductive reasoning paths from diverse domains.
TaDFM is a foundation model designed to internalize generalizable deductive logic for zero-shot tabular anomaly annotation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the coarse-to-fine annotation pipeline as novel and introduce TaDGeneral and TaDFM as new components of the approach.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on public and large-scale real-world tabular anomaly detection datasets reportedly show that TaDFM outperforms representative methods.
An industrial case study reportedly provides further validation of TaDFM's practical value.

narrative_sequence.summary: Tabular anomaly detection is important for securing real-world applications, but label annotation cost limits production scalability.
The paper proposes a coarse-to-fine annotation pipeline using LLMs for coarse annotation and humans for fine verification.
LLM generalization is limited by weak deductive grounding and single-domain fine-tuning overfitting.
TaDGeneral supplies cross-domain deductive reasoning paths, and TaDFM builds on them as a foundation model for zero-shot annotation.
The authors report comparative dataset experiments and an industrial case study supporting the approach.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset sizes, evaluation metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the annotation pipeline's operational costs or human-verification workload.
The abstract does not provide ablations separating the effects of TaDGeneral and TaDFM.
